incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD#789012 fired for service=redwood-serving, region=us-west-1a. symptom=queue_depth>500 AND p95_latency>1.5s. auto-page on-call.

kevin (sre-oncall): Acked PD#789012. I can see a sudden rise in kv-cache evictions on a subset of pods and backlog on the batch-queue. Starting triage.

maria (eng-runtime): Copy. Looking at metrics — GPU utilization normal, but host-side CPU and network TX are spiking for the serving nodes in us-west-1a-az2. Might be a network interface flapping.

sam (platform): @kevin can you confirm if autoscaler is suppressing new instances? I see scale-down inhibited but not scaling up.

kevin (sre-oncall): Autoscaler shows scaling attempts but K8s pending pods stuck in ContainerCreating with error: 
```
Warning FailedAttachVolume  kubelet, us-west-1a-node-12  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "vol-0a1b2c" : rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to attach
```
Looks like EBS attach timeouts in that AZ.

jess (support): We're already getting customer pings: a few enterprise customers reporting 502s for embeddings and chat generation. Flagging potential customer impact.

maria (eng-runtime): If EBS attach is slow, that would explain pending pods and queue backlog. We should activate regional fallback routing to us-west-2 for new traffic. Recommend flip routing policy to prefer us-west-2 for model variants with warmed caches.

sam (platform): I can push a temporary routing change. Plan: enable fallback routing rule "regional-pref: us-west-2" for 30m and enable deploy of a small warm-pool in us-west-2 (4 GPUs) for critical models. Thoughts?

kevin (sre-oncall): Do it. Also enable degraded-mode to disable long-tail batching to reduce latency. Command to update routing:
```
# enable fallback to us-west-2
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/routing/overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMP_OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"scope":"us-west-1","prefer":"us-west-2","ttl":1800}'
```

maria (eng-runtime): I'll trigger degraded-mode on the serving layer:
```
./bin/serving-cli set-config --degraded true --disable-batching=true --kv-cache-size=small
```
This prevents long tail formation while we move traffic.

incident-bot: PD#789012 acknowledged by kevin (sre-oncall) at 1999999999. Escalation timer paused.

kevin (sre-oncall): Routing override applied. Confirmed traffic shift: 62% of new sessions now landing in us-west-2. Queue depth in us-west-1a dropping.

jess (support): Notifying impacted customers with status note: "We are seeing degraded performance in us-west-1; traffic is being rerouted to us-west-2. You may see transient errors while we stabilize. No data loss expected."

sam (platform): Warm-pool spinup in us-west-2 started, 4 GPU nodes provisioning. ETA ~6m.

maria (eng-runtime): Observability: p95 in us-west-1a down from 1.7s -> 0.9s in 3m after routing change. Overall errors reduced by ~78% for affected endpoints. Good.

kevin (sre-oncall): Great. I'll keep PD open until primary AZ has stable pod attach behavior and pending queue drained. Posting current action items: 1) Platform to keep fallback routing until EBS attach error rate <1% for 10m. 2) Infra to engage cloud provider for EBS attach failures in us-west-1a. 3) Eng-runtime to run cache warm-up in us-west-2 and monitor quality regression.

sam (platform): Reached out to cloud support ticket CS-4521 referencing attach errors. They responded: "Investigating a partial control-plane degradation in us-west-1a affecting volume attachments."

jess (support): Sent targeted customer update to enterprise customers affected. Keeping public status page note minimal for now.

maria (eng-runtime): Running a sanity check on outputs from warm-pool — quality looks within baseline. No rollout required.

incident-bot: PD#789012 status changed: acknowledged -> investigating.

kevin (sre-oncall): After 28 minutes, attach failure rate still elevated but queue drained to safe levels. I recommend keeping routing override for 30 more minutes, then slowly relax. If attach failures persist beyond 90m we need a longer failover plan.

sam (platform): Extended override TTL to 3600s. We've also disabled canary routing to ensure stable distribution.

jess (support): Customer impact summary for post-incident: ~3% of requests in us-west region experienced 502s for ~25 minutes; mitigation via routing reduced impact within 7 minutes of activation.

kevin (sre-oncall): Thanks team. I'll mark PD with note and leave it open until cloud confirms resolution. Follow-up: schedule postmortem with infra and runtime tomorrow 10:00am PT.

maria (eng-runtime): I'll collect traces and prompt-level evals for potential regressions and include them in the postmortem.

incident-bot: PD#789012 updated: note added by kevin (sre-oncall).

kevin (sre-oncall): Closing interim thread here. If anything flares up ping me directly. :thumbsup:
